items.Sentence: Fine Screening: Secondary treated wastewater from OC San’s RP-1 is strained, or passed through rotating band fine-mesh screens, and chlorinated (as needed) prior to microfiltration.
Screenings are dewatered and returned to OC San for disposal.

Microfiltration: Screened secondary effluent flows via gravity to 26 in-basin microfiltration (MF) cells containing submerged racks of hollow fiber membranes with a maximum pore size of 0.2 micron. Sodium hypochlorite is added as needed to the MF feed to form a low level (3-5 mg/L) of chloramine to reduce/prevent fouling of the MF membranes. The waste backwash is returned to OC San for treatment.
Reverse Osmosis. The RO process will be bypassed when AWPF effluent is discharged to the Santa Ana River.

Advanced Oxidation/UV Disinfection: The advanced oxidation/disinfection process (AOP) consists of two steps: hydrogen peroxide addition and ultraviolet (UV) light treatment. UV irradiation is used for disinfection and reduction of light-sensitive contaminants.
Decarbonation and Lime Stabilization Process: This treatment process will be bypassed when AWPF effluent is discharged to the SAR.

Dechlorination and pH adjustment: After UV disinfection and prior to discharge to the SAR, the effluent stream may still contain some chloramines. Sodium bisulfate will be added for dechlorination, if needed.
